notes: RBox revision of the topic's symmetry slot (RBOX_PER_TOPIC: symmetry): sibling_of (tagged symmetric) loses symmetry; the paired contraction (people-delete-0010) removes the same property. The old edit made the relation 'asymmetric', and the models did not read that word: 3 of 4 answered 'yes' to 'Is sibling of asymmetric?' before editing, 3 of 4 missed the negation and the disjunction, and 3 of 4 called 'is married to' asymmetric. The edit now states the property in plain words, 'one person can be a sibling of another without the second being a sibling of the first' (axiom ¬Sym), and the direct question asks exactly that (no, then yes). Instances changed: Prince William and Prince Harry, and Venus and Serena Williams, are famous pairs whose converse is stored, so a model could answer from memory against a perfect edit. They are replaced by real but minor brothers: Ludwig Emil Grimm, the painter brother of Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, and the Bach sons Johann Christoph Friedrich and Johann Christian. Yes and no: the first instance (and the cross-lingual queries) asks whether the converse could fail given only the fact (no, then yes), the second whether it follows (yes, then no). Near asks the same plain-words symmetry question of another people relation (marriage, reference no; a leak turns it to yes); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1), as the template does.
